questions.q: Which four pillars of health does Chatterjee describe?
questions.why: The overview names the four habits the book builds its plan around.

questions.q: What single change does the summary say nearly every diet could use?
a: Eating more protein at every meal
Fasting for a full day each week
questions.why: Lesson 1 says doctors agree we consume far too much sugar, whatever diet we follow.

questions.q: What should you look for on labels to spot hidden sugar?
questions.why: Lesson 1 warns that sugar is disguised under many names, and the -ose ending is one clue.

questions.q: Which word does Chatterjee suggest using instead of exercise?
questions.why: Lesson 2 wants us to speak of movement, so daily motion matters more than formal workouts.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest judging the quality of your sleep?
a: By whether you wake refreshed and at a regular time
By counting the hours you spend in bed
By how quickly you fall asleep after lunch
By how vivid your dreams were that night
questions.why: Lesson 3 offers three checks, including waking without an alarm and feeling rested.
